title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes
content:
Summary:
Quick scratchpad capturing commands tried, observed errors, hypotheses and next steps for the intermittent streaming response breakage (SSE/chunking/backpressure) seen from hosted API (reported by customer A). Repro rate ~20% locally, much higher in Canary under load.

Context / Symptoms:
- Client receives partial SSE stream and then stalls; connection stays open for a long time (~30s) with no bytes. Eventually client times out or server logs a client disconnected write error.
- Occurs on text streaming endpoints (chat/generate) when responses are long and concurrent QPS high.
- Affected path: hosted-api -> edge proxy (nginx ELB) -> runtime (node/golang) -> model worker (gpt-like).

Most common log snippets observed:
- runtime: "write EPIPE" or "broken pipe" on write() after long idle
- proxy: "upstream timed out" or noted "client closed connection"
- model-worker: long GC pauses not correlated (cpu steady).

Commands used to repro: (run from devbox, replace HOST and API_KEY)
1) Simple curl SSE test (no buffering):
   curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://$HOST/v1/streams/generate?model=test-stream-1"
   Notes: -N to disable curl buffering. Repro intermittently. When reproduces, stream yields 2-3 events then nothing.

2) Curl with --no-buffer and increased verbosity to see bytes:
   curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://$HOST/v1/streams/generate?model=test-stream-1&max_tokens=1024"

3) Node quick client using eventsource / fetch:
   // node-fetch stream reading draft (used to test chunk boundaries)
   const res = await fetch(url, {headers});
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   while(true){ const {value, done} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; console.log('chunk len', value.length);}
   Observed: reader.read() hangs (pending) after a few chunks in repro case.

4) Python aiohttp client (async):
   session.get(url) as resp:
       async for line in resp.content:
           print(len(line))
   Observed identical hanging behavior.

Server-side toggles tried in staging (quick changes):
- nginx: set proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on.
  Result: slight improvement; some previously hanging repros moved to complete, but not eliminated under load.
- nginx: add header X-Accel-Buffering: no on responses.
  Result: same as above.
- Increased keepalive_timeout and proxy_read_timeout to 120s. No clear effect on root cause.
- Disabled HTTP/2 on ALB -> forced HTTP/1.1. No repro change observed locally.

Runtime code investigations and changed flags:
- Flushed stdout / response writer after sending each chunk (call flush in golang and res.flush() in node).
  Observed that explicit flush reduces frequency, which suggests buffering path involved.
- Disabled internal batching (continuous batching) for this endpoint to force immediate send. Result: lower repro but increases cost.
- Added periodic heartbeats (":

") to SSE stream every 3s to prevent idle timeouts. This reduced the occurrence in some cases but not all.

Error traces captured (representative):
- runtime.log 2025-10-11T15:34:10Z ERROR write failed: write tcp 10.0.8.14:443->10.0.3.22:56324: write: broken pipe
- proxy.log 2025-10-11T15:34:12Z WARN upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Proxy/edge buffering + HTTP keepalive interplay: some intermediate proxy decides stream is idle (because chunk sizes are < N bytes) and buffers/discards until closed. Heartbeat reduced but did not eliminate.
2) Backpressure from downstream consumer (model worker) causes response writer to see EPIPE when buffer limits hit and client disconnects; but client reports hanging not immediate close.
3) Nagle/packet coalescing leading to micro-bursts that some proxies treat as closed stream (edge bug).
4) TLS record size or ALPN HTTP/2 framing differences between client and internal path causing chunk boundary mis-detection (less likely).

Repro matrix attempted:
- Client types: curl (Linux/mac), node-fetch, aiohttp, browser EventSource (Chrome). Hanging occurs across clients.
- Edge vs Direct to runtime: Direct-to-runtime (bypassing nginx in staging) reduces repro frequency dramatically -> points to proxy/buffer interaction.
- Small chunks vs big chunks: when we combine tokens into larger chunks (send >1KB per event), repro decreases.

Temporary mitigations already deployed to Canary: (did not fully resolve)
- Set proxy_buffering off and X-Accel-Buffering: no in edge.
- Implement server-side periodic SSE comments (":\n") every 2s until full chunk arrives.
- On failing paths, fallback to polling API for customers showing persistent failures.

Next debugging steps (actionable):
- Reproduce with tcpdump on both sides to observe packet-level flow during hanging scenario. Capture both sides: edge->runtime and client->edge.
- Add additional size/timing telemetry to runtime: log timestamp + bytecount for each chunk sent and flush calls to correlate with proxy logs. Use structured traces with request_id.
- Try replicating with a minimal nginx config locally (no ALB) to see if ALB contributes.
- Experiment: set sendfile off, tcp_nodelay on, tcp_nopush off in nginx/runtime sockets.
- Ask infra to temporarily route a failing tenant through a debug-enabled proxy that logs buffering behavior.

Open questions to triage with infra and networking teams:
- Are there any middleboxes (WAF, CDN) that could be re-chunking or buffering SSE?
- ALB/NGINX versions and known bugs for chunked transfer + keepalive interactions?
- Any TLS termination differences causing delayed flushes?

Notes from Slack thread #streaming-bugs (copied snippets):
- Liam: "I was able to repro reliably when two clients streamed to the same runtime pod at ~80% GPU util. Might be shared write buffer starvation."
- Ravi: "Turning off request buffering in nginx helped for me. Also saw a 503 once with ALB when bursts happened."

Immediate experiment to run (low effort):
- Run the Node client with --no-buffer to ensure client not aggregating. Launch small python script that opens 50 concurrent eventsource connections to staging runtime directly (bypass ALB) and observe success vs failure rate with and without server heartbeats.

Notes for the ticket INC-4211:
- Attach tcpdump pcap of a failing session, runtime debug logs with per-chunk timing, nginx debug logs for the same request_id. Add before/after of config changes.

Personal TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add per-chunk telemetry (done: low-detail logs)
- [ ] Schedule packet capture with infra (in progress)
- [ ] Run large-scale repro harness (50-200 conns) direct-to-runtime and via ALB
- [ ] Validate if switching ALB -> NLB changes behavior

If anyone else reproduces, paste exact curl command and runtime request_id in this doc.

End of notes.
